NASB.1: 'At that time the LORD said to me, 'Cut out for yourself two tablets of stone like the former ones, and come up to Me on the mountain, and make an ark of wood for yourself.
NASB.2: 'I will write on the tablets the words that were on the former tablets which you shattered, and you shall put them in the ark.'
NASB.3: 'So I made an ark of acacia wood and cut out two tablets of stone like the former ones, and went up on the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
NASB.4: 'He wrote on the tablets, like the former writing, the Ten Commandments which the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly; and the LORD gave them to me.
NASB.5: 'Then I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark which I had made; and there they are, as the LORD commanded me.'
NASB.6: (Now the sons of Israel set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and there he was buried and Eleazar his son ministered as priest in his place.
NASB.7: From there they set out to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of brooks of water.
NASB.8: At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to serve Him and to bless in His name until this day.
NASB.9: Therefore, Levi does not have a portion or inheritance with his brothers; the LORD is his inheritance, just as the LORD your God spoke to him.)
NASB.10: 'I, moreover, stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights like the first time, and the LORD listened to me that time also; the LORD was not willing to destroy you.
NASB.11: 'Then the LORD said to me, 'Arise, proceed on your journey ahead of the people, that they may go in and possess the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.'
NASB.12: 'Now, Israel, what does the LORD your God require from you, but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways and love Him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
NASB.13: [and] to keep the LORD'S commandments and His statutes which I am commanding you today for your good?
NASB.14: 'Behold, to the LORD your God belong heaven and the highest heavens, the earth and all that is in it.
NASB.15: 'Yet on your fathers did the LORD set His affection to love them, and He chose their descendants after them, [even] you above all peoples, as [it is] this day.
NASB.16: 'So circumcise your heart, and stiffen your neck no longer.
NASB.17: 'For the LORD your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God who does not show partiality nor take a bribe.
NASB.18: 'He executes justice for the orphan and the widow, and shows His love for the alien by giving him food and clothing.
NASB.19: 'So show your love for the alien, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
NASB.20: 'You shall fear the LORD your God; you shall serve Him and cling to Him, and you shall swear by His name.
NASB.21: 'He is your praise and He is your God, who has done these great and awesome things for you which your eyes have seen.
NASB.22: 'Your fathers went down to Egypt seventy persons [in all], and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven.

NKJV.1: “At that time the LORD said to me, ‘Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to Me on the mountain and make yourself an ark of wood.
NKJV.2: And I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke; and you shall put them in the ark.’
NKJV.3: “So I made an ark of acacia wood, hewed two tablets of stone like the first, and went up the mountain, having the two tablets in my hand.
NKJV.4: And He wrote on the tablets according to the first writing, the Ten Commandments, which the LORD had spoken to you in the mountain from the midst of the fire in the day of the assembly; and the LORD gave them to me.
NKJV.5: Then I turned and came down from the mountain, and put the tablets in the ark which I had made; and there they are, just as the LORD commanded me.”
NKJV.6: (Now the children of Israel journeyed from the wells of Bene Jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died, and where he was buried; and Eleazar his son ministered as priest in his stead.
NKJV.7: From there they journeyed to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of rivers of water.
NKJV.8: At that time the LORD separated the tribe of Levi to bear the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to minister to Him and to bless in His name, to this day.
NKJV.9: Therefore Levi has no portion nor inheritance with his brethren; the LORD is his inheritance, just as the LORD your God promised him.)
NKJV.10: “As at the first time, I stayed in the mountain forty days and forty nights; the LORD also heard me at that time, and the LORD chose not to destroy you.
NKJV.11: Then the LORD said to me, ‘Arise, begin your journey before the people, that they may go in and possess the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.’
NKJV.12: “And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God require of you, but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways and to love Him, to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
NKJV.13: and to keep the commandments of the LORD and His statutes which I command you today for your good?
NKJV.14: Indeed heaven and the highest heavens belong to the LORD your God, also the earth with all that is in it.
NKJV.15: The LORD delighted only in your fathers, to love them; and He chose their descendants after them, you above all peoples, as it is this day.
NKJV.16: Therefore circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and be stiff-necked no longer.
NKJV.17: For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, mighty and awesome, who shows no partiality nor takes a bribe.
NKJV.18: He administers justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the stranger, giving him food and clothing.
NKJV.19: Therefore love the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
NKJV.20: You shall fear the LORD your God; you shall serve Him, and to Him you shall hold fast, and take oaths in His name.
NKJV.21: He is your praise, and He is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things which your eyes have seen.
NKJV.22: Your fathers went down to Egypt with seventy persons, and now the LORD your God has made you as the stars of heaven in multitude.

ESV.1: “At that time the LORD said to me, ‘Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to me on the mountain and make an ark of wood.
ESV.2: And I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets that you broke, and you shall put them in the ark.’
ESV.3: So I made an ark of acacia wood, and cut two tablets of stone like the first, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
ESV.4: And he wrote on the tablets, in the same writing as before, the Ten Commandments  that the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly. And the LORD gave them to me.
ESV.5: Then I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark that I had made. And there they are, as the LORD commanded me.”
ESV.6: (The people of Israel journeyed from Beeroth Bene-jaakan  to Moserah. There Aaron died, and there he was buried. And his son Eleazar ministered as priest in his place.
ESV.7: From there they journeyed to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with brooks of water.
ESV.8: At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD to stand before the LORD to minister to him and to bless in his name, to this day.
ESV.9: Therefore Levi has no portion or inheritance with his brothers. The LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God said to him.)
ESV.10: “I myself stayed on the mountain, as at the first time, forty days and forty nights, and the LORD listened to me that time also. The LORD was unwilling to destroy you.
ESV.11: And the LORD said to me, ‘Arise, go on your journey at the head of the people, so that they may go in and possess the land, which I swore to their fathers to give them.’
ESV.12: “And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God require of you, but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
ESV.13: and to keep the commandments and statutes of the LORD, which I am commanding you today for your good?
ESV.14: Behold, to the LORD your God belong heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth with all that is in it.
ESV.15: Yet the LORD set his heart in love on your fathers and chose their offspring after them, you above all peoples, as you are this day.
ESV.16: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no longer stubborn.
ESV.17: For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who is not partial and takes no bribe.
ESV.18: He executes justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the sojourner, giving him food and clothing.
ESV.19: Love the sojourner, therefore, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
ESV.20: You shall fear the LORD your God. You shall serve him and hold fast to him, and by his name you shall swear.
ESV.21: He is your praise. He is your God, who has done for you these great and terrifying things that your eyes have seen.
ESV.22: Your fathers went down to Egypt seventy persons, and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven.

CSB17.1: “The LORD said to me at that time, ‘Cut two stone tablets like the first ones and come to me on the mountain and make a wooden ark.
CSB17.2: I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets you broke, and you are to place them in the ark.’
CSB17.3: So I made an ark of acacia wood, <sup>ⓗ</sup> cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and climbed the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
CSB17.4: Then on the day of the assembly, the LORD wrote on the tablets what had been written previously, the Ten Commandments that he had spoken to you on the mountain from the fire. The LORD gave them to me,
CSB17.5: and I went back down the mountain and placed the tablets in the ark I had made. And they have remained there, as the LORD commanded me.” <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.6: The Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene-jaakan <sup>[1]</sup> to Moserah. Aaron died and was buried there, and Eleazar his son became priest in his place. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.7: They traveled from there to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with flowing streams. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.8: “At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi <sup>ⓛ</sup> to carry the ark of the LORD’s covenant, to stand before the LORD to serve him, and to pronounce blessings in his name, as it is today.
CSB17.9: For this reason, Levi does not have a portion or inheritance like his brothers; the LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God told him. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.10: “I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights like the first time. The LORD also listened to me on this occasion; <sup>ⓝ</sup> he agreed not to annihilate you.
CSB17.11: Then the LORD said to me, ‘Get up. Continue your journey ahead of the people, so that they may enter and possess the land I swore to give their fathers.’ <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.12: “And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you except to fear <sup>ⓑ</sup> the LORD your God by walking in all his ways, to love him, and to worship the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul? <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.13: Keep the LORD’s commands and statutes I am giving you today, for your own good. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.14: The heavens, indeed the highest heavens, belong to the LORD your God, as does the earth and everything in it. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.15: Yet the LORD had his heart set on your fathers and loved them. <sup>ⓕ</sup> He chose their descendants after them — he chose you out of all the peoples, as it is today. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.16: Therefore, circumcise your hearts <sup>ⓗ</sup> and don’t be stiff-necked any longer.
CSB17.17: For the LORD your God is the God of gods <sup>ⓘ</sup> and Lord of lords, <sup>ⓙ</sup> the great, mighty, and awe-inspiring God, showing no partiality and taking no bribe. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.18: He executes justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the resident alien, giving him food and clothing. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.19: You are also to love the resident alien, since you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.20: You are to fear the LORD your God and worship him. Remain faithful <sup>[2]</sup> to him and take oaths in his name. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.21: He is your praise and he is your God, who has done for you these great and awe-inspiring works your eyes have seen.
CSB17.22: Your fathers went down to Egypt, seventy people in all, <sup>ⓐ</sup> and now the LORD your God has made you numerous, like the stars of the sky. <sup>ⓑ</sup>

WEB.1: At that time Yahweh said to me, “Cut two stone tablets like the first, and come up to me onto the mountain, and make an ark of wood.
WEB.2: I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets which you broke, and you shall put them in the ark.”
WEB.3: So I made an ark of acacia wood, and cut two stone tablets like the first, and went up onto the mountain, having the two tablets in my hand.
WEB.4: He wrote on the tablets, according to the first writing, the ten commandments, which Yahweh spoke to you on the mountain out of the middle of the fire in the day of the assembly: and Yahweh gave them to me.
WEB.5: I turned and came down from the mountain, and put the tablets in the ark which I had made; and there they are as Yahweh commanded me.
WEB.6: (The children of Israel traveled from Beeroth Bene Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died, and there he was buried; and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest’s office in his place.
WEB.7: From there they traveled to Gudgodah; and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of brooks of water.
WEB.8: At that time Yahweh set apart the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of Yahweh’s covenant, to stand before Yahweh to minister to him, and to bless in his name, to this day.
WEB.9: Therefore Levi has no portion nor inheritance with his brothers; Yahweh is his inheritance, according as Yahweh your God spoke to him.)
WEB.10: I stayed on the mountain, as at the first time, forty days and forty nights: and Yahweh listened to me that time also; Yahweh would not destroy you.
WEB.11: Yahweh said to me, “Arise, take your journey before the people; and they shall go in and possess the land, which I swore to their fathers to give to them.”
WEB.12: Now, Israel, what does Yahweh your God require of you, but to fear Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
WEB.13: to keep Yahweh’s commandments and statutes, which I command you today for your good?
WEB.14: Behold, to Yahweh your God belongs heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth, with all that is therein.
WEB.15: Only Yahweh had a delight in your fathers to love them, and he chose their offspring  after them, even you above all peoples, as it is today.
WEB.16: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiff-necked.
WEB.17: For Yahweh your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons, nor takes reward.
WEB.18: He does execute justice for the fatherless and widow, and loves the foreigner, in giving him food and clothing.
WEB.19: Therefore love the foreigner; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
WEB.20: You shall fear Yahweh your God; you shall serve him; and you shall cling to him, and you shall swear by his name.
WEB.21: He is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things, which your eyes have seen.
WEB.22: Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy persons; and now Yahweh your God has made you as the stars of the sky for multitude.

NLT.1: “At that time the LORD said to me, ‘Chisel out two stone tablets like the first ones. Also make a wooden Ark — a sacred chest to store them in. Come up to me on the mountain,
NLT.2: and I will write on the tablets the same words that were on the ones you smashed. Then place the tablets in the Ark.’
NLT.3: “So I made an Ark of acacia wood and cut two stone tablets like the first two. Then I went up the mountain with the tablets in my hand.
NLT.4: Once again the LORD wrote the Ten Commandments on the tablets and gave them to me. They were the same words the LORD had spoken to you from the heart of the fire on the day you were assembled at the foot of the mountain.
NLT.5: Then I turned and came down the mountain and placed the tablets in the Ark of the Covenant, which I had made, just as the LORD commanded me. And the tablets are still there in the Ark.”
NLT.6: (The people of Israel set out from the wells of the people of Jaakan and traveled to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried. His son Eleazar ministered as high priest in his place.
NLT.7: Then they journeyed to Gudgodah, and from there to Jotbathah, a land with many brooks and streams.
NLT.8: At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the Ark of the LORD’s Covenant, and to stand before the LORD as his ministers, and to pronounce blessings in his name. These are their duties to this day.
NLT.9: That is why the Levites have no share of property or possession of land among the other Israelite tribes. The LORD himself is their special possession, as the LORD your God told them.)
NLT.10: “As for me, I stayed on the mountain in the LORD’s presence for forty days and nights, as I had done the first time. And once again the LORD listened to my pleas and agreed not to destroy you.
NLT.11: Then the LORD said to me, ‘Get up and resume the journey, and lead the people to the land I swore to give to their ancestors, so they may take possession of it.’
NLT.12: “And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God require of you? He requires only that you fear the LORD your God, and live in a way that pleases him, and love him and serve him with all your heart and soul.
NLT.13: And you must always obey the LORD’s commands and decrees that I am giving you today for your own good.
NLT.14: “Look, the highest heavens and the earth and everything in it all belong to the LORD your God.
NLT.15: Yet the LORD chose your ancestors as the objects of his love. And he chose you, their descendants, above all other nations, as is evident today.
NLT.16: Therefore, change your hearts and stop being stubborn.
NLT.17: “For the LORD your God is the God of gods and Lord of lords. He is the great God, the mighty and awesome God, who shows no partiality and cannot be bribed.
NLT.18: He ensures that orphans and widows receive justice. He shows love to the foreigners living among you and gives them food and clothing.
NLT.19: So you, too, must show love to foreigners, for you yourselves were once foreigners in the land of Egypt.
NLT.20: You must fear the LORD your God and worship him and cling to him. Your oaths must be in his name alone.
NLT.21: He alone is your God, the only one who is worthy of your praise, the one who has done these mighty miracles that you have seen with your own eyes.
NLT.22: When your ancestors went down into Egypt, there were only seventy of them. But now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the sky!

AMP.1: "At that time the LORD said to me, 'Cut out for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to Me on the mountain, and make an ark (chest) of wood for yourself.
AMP.2: I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets which you shattered, and you shall put them in the ark.'
AMP.3: So I made an ark of acacia wood and cut out two tablets of stone like the first, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
AMP.4: The LORD wrote on the tablets, like the first writing, the Ten Commandments which the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly; then the LORD gave them to me.
AMP.5: Then I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark which I had made; and they are there, just as the LORD commanded me."

AMP.22: Your fathers went down to Egypt, seventy persons [in all], and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven.

NIV.1:
Tablets Like the First Ones
At that time the Lord said to me, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the first ones and come up to me on the mountain. Also make a wooden chest.
NIV.2: I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke. Then you are to put them in the chest.”
NIV.3: So I made the ark out of acacia wood and chiseled out two stone tablets like the first ones, and I went up on the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.
NIV.4: The Lord wrote on these tablets what he had written before, the Ten Commandments he had proclaimed to you on the mountain, out of the fire, on the day of the assembly. And the Lord gave them to me.
NIV.5: Then I came back down the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I had made, as the Lord commanded me, and they are there now.
NIV.6: (The Israelites traveled from the wells of the Jaakanites to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son succeeded him as priest.
NIV.7: From there they traveled to Gudgodah and on to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water.
NIV.8: At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to minister and to pronounce blessings in his name, as they still do today.
NIV.9: That is why the Levites have no share or inheritance among their brothers; the Lord is their inheritance, as the Lord your God told them.)
NIV.10: Now I had stayed on the mountain forty days and nights, as I did the first time, and the Lord listened to me at this time also. It was not his will to destroy you.
NIV.11: “Go,” the Lord said to me, “and lead the people on their way, so that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.”
NIV.12:
Fear the Lord
And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
NIV.13: and to observe the Lord’s commands and decrees that I am giving you today for your own good?
NIV.14: To the Lord your God belong the heavens, even the highest heavens, the earth and everything in it.
NIV.15: Yet the Lord set his affection on your forefathers and loved them, and he chose you, their descendants, above all the nations, as it is today.
NIV.16: Circumcise your hearts, therefore, and do not be stiff-necked any longer.
NIV.17: For the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, mighty and awesome, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribes.
NIV.18: He defends the cause of the fatherless and the widow, and loves the alien, giving him food and clothing.
NIV.19: And you are to love those who are aliens, for you yourselves were aliens in Egypt.
NIV.20: Fear the Lord your God and serve him. Hold fast to him and take your oaths in his name.
NIV.21: He is your praise; he is your God, who performed for you those great and awesome wonders you saw with your own eyes.
NIV.22: Your forefathers who went down into Egypt were seventy in all, and now the Lord your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the sky.
